newsitem.title: POLAND: FBI opens office in Poland.
newsitem.headline: FBI opens office in Poland.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) opened an office in Warsaw on Thursday to cooperate with Polish police in the fight against organised crime.
"This is a testimony to very good relations between the Polish and American police services," Polish Interior Minister Leszek Miller told a news briefing.

The office's head, Polish-born Andrzej Zawitkowski, said cooperation with the Polish police would focus on fighting international terrorism, car thefts and white collar crime, such as bank frauds and money laundering.
Poland has seen organised crime mounting since the fall of communism in 1989, when it liberalised travel regulations and curbed police powers, often abused under the old system.
Police analysts are concerned criminal groups from theformer Soviet Union are using Poland as a conduit to Western Europe.
